findings.title: no-new-findings compares against prior INDEPENDENT passes only; spec says 'same-gate prior passes' (includes in-context)
findings.recommendation: evaluateReviewed computes the new-finding comparison set as `priorIndep = independents.slice(0, -1)` — only prior independent-class passes. orbit-engine-gates spec.md:132-134 says a new finding is matched against 'same-gate prior passes only' (all prior passes for the gate, including in-context). Verified: gates.ts:175 vs spec:132-134. Impact: if an in-context pass surfaced finding X and a later independent pass re-surfaces X, the code flags X as new (fails no-new-findings, extra cycle) though the spec treats it as not-new. Largely inert for the shipped proposal cadence [independent, in-context] (independent comes first, no prior in-context), but a real deviation and would bite a cadence with an in-context slot before the independent one. No test distinguishes (gates.test.ts:237 has an empty prior set).

recommendation_options.label: A
recommendation_options.body: Fix the code: compare latestIndep against ALL same-gate passes preceding it (ordered.slice(0, ordered.indexOf(latestIndep))), not just prior independents

recommendation_options.label: B
recommendation_options.body: Amend orbit-engine-gates spec.md:133 to say 'prior independent-class passes' if the stricter loop is the intended semantics

findings.title: Gate reference-validation now hard-fails apply-only schemas with a dangling apply.requires (previously silently accepted)
findings.recommendation: validateGates runs whenever an apply: block is present and reference-checks the normalized apply gate's requires/inputs. Pre-C1, apply.requires was never reference-validated (only artifacts were), so a schema with apply:{requires:[typo]} parsed. It now throws. Valid upstream/XDG schemas are unaffected (test 4.1 confirms), so this is a defensible tightening, but it is an observable change for MALFORMED apply-only schemas — mildly in tension with the 'no behavior change is observable' phrasing. Recommend accepting as an intentional improvement and adding a one-line note to the 'Upstream apply: block normalized' requirement that apply.requires references are now validated.

findings.title: instructions apply blocked-by-gate is entry-gated (complete===0) — not stated in the spec scenario
findings.recommendation: The blocked-by-gate branch is guarded by `state === 'ready' && complete === 0` (dogfooding-added: post-apply the proposal gate is moot; don't re-block mid-implementation). Well-reasoned and consistent with design.md, but the spec scenario (orbit-engine-gates:220-223) says only 'runs while review-proposal is unpassed → state: blocked-by-gate' with no task-completion qualifier. Add a clause to the gate-aware instructions requirement noting apply's blocked-by-gate is entry-gated (fires only before any task is checked), so the spec matches shipped behavior.

findings.title: Position-readout render tokens ((past), unpassed) and declaration-order not documented in the spec
findings.recommendation: buildPositionReadout renders gates in declaration order only (spec.md:205 says 'Step order follows requires/before edges; ties by declaration order' — coincidentally correct for spec-driven, but an arbitrarily-ordered gated schema would render out of flow). renderGate emits a literal 'unpassed' and an undocumented '(past)' token for superseded gates (the dogfooding-added moot-gate feature), neither in the spec's enumerated render set (spec.md:200-208). Document the superseded '(past)' render + the 'unpassed' token + the superseded-gate concept in the position-readout / gate-aware-status requirement (the superseded concept isn't in the spec at all); topological sort by requires/before is a lower-priority generality improvement.
